name: Supademo
subcategory: screen recording, walkthroughs and product demos
tagline: Capture clicks and screenshots into an interactive walkthrough with editable annotations

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 creator/admin; 5 guided interactive demos; 50 4K recordings; unlimited views; 1080p watermarked exports

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.limits: Unlimited demos and recordings; 5 viewer collaborators; 1 workspace
tiers.notes: Annual discount is advertised, but the exact annual dollar rate was not exposed in parsed text. The supplied snapshot said $36/month for Pro; the current entry paid tier is Scale at $38/month.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: 5 creators included; unlimited viewers; HTML/sandbox demos and onboarding

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Starts at 10 creators; multiple workspaces; custom security, support and procurement

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 creator/admin, 5 guided interactive demos, 50 4K recordings, unlimited views and 1080p watermarked exports
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (advertised savings up to 33%); exact annual rates were not publicly extractable; 14-day paid trials
pricing.hiddenCosts: Growth includes only 5 creators and charges $50/month for each additional creator; AI Demo Agent is an add-on averaging about $0.50–$0.80 per qualified demo.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Supademo, capture clicks and screenshots into an interactive walkthrough with editable annotations. The hard boundary is hosted embeds, analytics, personalization, integrations, and team libraries, plus capture polish, hosting, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Capture clicks and screenshots into an interactive walkthrough, add editable annotations at key moments, and export a shareable local video.
whatYouLose: hosted embeds, analytics, personalization, integrations, and team libraries
ongoingBurden: OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Supademo because the recording itself is easy; the subscription removes upload, transcoding, sharing, organization, and support work. The recurring cost buys OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Cap
priorArt.desc: Open-source screen recording and sharing product with modern desktop architecture.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Propels
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Open-source in theory; 27 stars and an AWS Amplify development setup are not a product a non-builder installs.

rejectedAlternatives.name: rrweb
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The famous answer is an SDK and player, not an editable walkthrough product.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal desktop recorder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Supademo in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, ffmpeg, and SQLite; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: capture clicks and screenshots into an interactive walkthrough, add editable annotations at key moments, and export a shareable local video.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Offer screen, window, or region capture plus optional microphone audio.
Show an always-visible recording timer and make stop available from the tray.
Create a non-destructive trim view with crop, zoom, cursor highlight, and text callouts.
Render locally through ffmpeg with sensible H.264 and WebM presets.
Generate a poster frame, transcript, and Markdown summary beside each video.
Provide copy-file-path and reveal-in-folder actions instead of mandatory cloud upload.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out public cloud hosting.
Deliberately leave out viewer identity and engagement analytics.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workspaces and SSO.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
